GPU encoding on every vendor, and the rest of the web-desktop surface jlesage/handbrake has long offered. Set one variable and every watch-folder job is transcoded by the GPU instead of the CPU; browse, upload, run hooks and get notified from the same tab.

## ✨ Added

- **NVIDIA NVENC hardware encoding.** `GPU_VENDOR=nvidia` runs every automated watch-folder conversion on an NVIDIA GPU with HandBrake's NVENC encoder. The container needs the NVIDIA runtime (`--runtime=nvidia`), a GPU in `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,video,utility`, the README's Hardware Encoding section has the full Unraid recipe. This closes the gap the Alpine-based `jlesage/handbrake` cannot close at all, because NVIDIA's userspace libraries are glibc binaries that musl cannot load ([jlesage/docker-handbrake#49](https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake/issues/49), open since 2019).
- **Intel Quick Sync (QSV) hardware encoding.** `GPU_VENDOR=intel` with `--device /dev/dri` passed through runs conversions on an Intel iGPU or Arc card. Verified on real Intel UHD 770 hardware, at roughly 2.25x the software encoder's speed.
- **A real Ubuntu packaging bug found and fixed.** Ubuntu's `handbrake-cli` package detects QSV correctly but every real QSV conversion with it fails at the muxing step ([HandBrake/HandBrake#7962](https://github.com/HandBrake/HandBrake/issues/7962)). The optional `handbrake:gpu-full` image (built from `Dockerfile.gpu`, `just build-gpu-full`) rebuilds `HandBrakeCLI` from source with `--enable-qsv`, which fixes it completely, confirmed end to end on the same hardware. The same build adds AMD VCE support (`--enable-vce`), since Ubuntu never compiles that in at all.
- **An honest AMD VCE fallback.** `GPU_VENDOR=amd` on the standard image explains precisely why it is falling back to software (no AMD hardware encoder in the stock build) and names `handbrake:gpu-full` as the way to get it. AMD VCE itself remains unverified: there is no AMD GPU available to test on.
- **A GPU hardware report form.** Anyone with an Intel or AMD GPU can confirm their result through a structured issue form instead of writing a report from scratch.
- **Verification records.** `docs/hardware-encoding-nvidia.md` and `docs/hardware-encoding-intel.md` document which encoders each build actually contains, what the host has to provide, and the measured hardware runs behind every "verified" claim.
- **A web file manager.** `WEB_FILE_MANAGER=1` (the default) publishes the watch folders, the output folder and `/storage` at `https://<host>:3001/files/` for browsing, download and upload. On by default, unlike jlesage's opt-in equivalent, since anyone who can reach the WebUI already has a full desktop session with the same file access. `/config` is refused even if asked for explicitly, since it holds the WebUI's TLS private key.
- **A web terminal.** `WEB_TERMINAL=1` unlocks every terminal binary in the image and binds `Ctrl+Alt+T` to open one on the web desktop, needed because HandBrake's maximised window makes the openbox root menu unreachable otherwise.
- **Desktop notifications.** `WEB_NOTIFICATION=1` shows a popup on the web desktop when a conversion finishes or fails, through `dunst`.
- **Conversion hooks.** `pre_conversion.sh`, `post_conversion.sh`, `post_watch_folder_processing.sh` and `hb_custom_args.sh` in `/config/hooks/` run at the matching points in every conversion, with the same argument order `jlesage/handbrake` uses, so existing hook scripts keep working unchanged.
- **A configurable staging directory.** `AUTOMATED_CONVERSION_STAGING_DIR` moves in-progress conversions off the array while they run, then finalises them onto the output disk atomically. An unwritable staging directory now refuses to convert anything and says exactly why, instead of failing every file one by one.
- **Safe multi-instance operation.** Two containers can now share one watch folder to convert twice as many files at once; a lock directory per file keeps them from colliding, and each instance only ever cleans up its own leftovers after an unclean stop.
- **Optical-drive plumbing.** `ATTACHED_DEVICES_PERMS=/dev/sr*` activates the LinuxServer base's own device-group logic for a passed-through drive. Unverified: no optical drive was available to test a rip end to end.
- **Watch-folder directory exclusion.** `AUTOMATED_CONVERSION_IGNORE_DIRECTORIES` prunes named subdirectories, such as sync-client metadata folders, out of every scan. Requested against jlesage/docker-handbrake as [issue #77](https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake/issues/77) and as an [unmerged community PR](https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake/pull/262).
- **A daily active-hours window.** `AUTOMATED_CONVERSION_ACTIVE_HOURS` restricts automated conversion to a time range, e.g. `22-06` for overnight only, so a NAS is not competing with a transcode during the day.
- **A hook for manual GUI conversions.** `post_manual_conversion.sh` fires after a conversion started in the GUI itself finishes, not just the watch-folder daemon, using HandBrake's own "Send file to" preference. Requested against jlesage/docker-handbrake as [issue #446](https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake/issues/446) and never implemented there.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The GPU setting now tells the truth, for every vendor.** `GPU_VENDOR=nvidia`, `intel` or `amd` on a container that cannot actually use that hardware prints exactly which piece is missing, names the fix, and keeps converting in software instead of failing every file. Check it any time with `docker exec handbrake cat /run/handbrake/gpu-args`: empty means software. Full diagnostics land in `/config/handbrake-gpu.log`.
- **Disk-full is verified safe, not just assumed.** Tested against a real, size-limited output filesystem: a full disk fails the conversion cleanly, leaves nothing corrupt behind, and never deletes or marks the source done, unlike a confirmed opposite-direction bug in jlesage/docker-handbrake ([issue #435](https://github.com/jlesage/docker-handbrake/issues/435)).

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The file manager rejected every path as unsafe.** A newline-safety check compared paths against `$(printf '\n')`, which command substitution silently reduces to an empty string, matching and rejecting absolutely everything. Caught on the very first real boot before release.
- **A single denied path was silently ignored.** `WEB_FILE_MANAGER_DENIED_PATHS` with exactly one entry (no comma) fed a `while read` loop an unterminated line, which bash drops instead of processing. Both fixes were found through real container boots, not just lint, before anything shipped.
